quest.title: Soloist's Prologue
quest.description: It is time to go to Fontaine, it seems. The next phase of your journey is about to begin...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1000, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

talks.objective: Go to Caravan Ribat

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good ol' Caravan Ribat. Huh, now let Paimon think... What were we up to the first time we came here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon remembers... Nahida's consciousness had been trapped by The Doctor, but we followed the clues she left behind to help her!

choices.text: Good memory, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So much time has already passed since then, and it seems Sumeru's changing for the better now that Nahida's in charge, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon just hopes this peace will last a long time, and then Nahida won't have any more new problems to deal with.

choices.text: Yes, but as long as we're around...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, guess you're right... We somehow always find ourselves right in the thick of it... Who knows what will happen next!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come to think of it, maybe it's all because of you... Maybe you're just a magnet for trouble!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I was just thinking that you might be the problem, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Me!? Before Paimon ran into you, Paimon never ran into any trouble! At most, when she was super tired, Paimon got caught in some strange whirlpool and sucked out to sea! And even then, you fished Paimon out!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, anyway... For Nahida's sake, maybe we should think about heading to our next destination for now.

choices.text: Next stop: Fontaine.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Ah, look who it is. Running into you in a place like this, I can see you two still love wandering around.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, it's Dehya! Since when are we just "wandering around"? We're usually taking care of some serious business... Even though it may have nothing to do with our journey...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But never mind that... What brings you here?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I just finished a commission in the desert for a usual client of mine. Nothing too interesting... just escorting a shipment of goods. I'm on my way to report back.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: That's when I saw you two all the way over there, chatting away. What were you two talking about, anyway?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We're preparing to leave Sumeru and head to Fontaine.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Huh? You serious...?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Can't say I saw that coming... *sigh* But you are travelers, after all. I guess you'd never stay for too long in one place.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Bumping into you like this will become a rarity. Ah, I'm starting to feel sad just thinking about it.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Hey, how about I gather a few mercs to escort you two... Whaddya say?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thanks, but no need. Paimon had no clue you'd miss us so much. But don't worry, we'll come back to see everyone when we get a chance!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Sounds good! All you need to do to get to Fontaine is cross this stretch of desert and navigate some waterways. Knowing you two, I'm sure it won't be anything you can't handle.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: So, when are ya leaving?

choices.text: We'll leave as soon as we've finished a few more preparations.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, wait a sec... Paimon just remembered there are still a few dishes in Sumeru that Paimon hasn't tried yet. Now where's that list Paimon made...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I see. Guess you won't be needing a going away party or anything. It's sad enough to see you go like this.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Though now that I think about it, Sumeru wouldn't be what it is today without you. Seems true heroes always prefer leaving quietly, haha.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By the way, should we go say bye to Nahida?

choices.text: In her case...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, good point. Then there's no need to bother her in the real world.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: #Then I guess this is goodbye for now, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. Whether as a client or a friend, you're always welcome to come find me.

choices.text: Take care.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Goodbye, Dehya! Bye bye, Sumeru!

choices.text: Bye, Dehya.
She'll know from our dreams anyway.
Journeys should be spontaneous.
Alright, let's continue our journey.
It's hard to say what will happen...
I guess we may have stumbled upon this place at some point before.

talks.objective: Go to Romaritime Harbor in Fontaine

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, after crossing all that sand and water, we finally made it... This must be Fontaine's port.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, everything looks so advanced in Fontaine. Paimon's heard that the industry here is extremely developed, and there are all kinds of unusual machines.

choices.text: So I heard, and it's about what I imagined.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just seeing the sights as tourists is nice, but maybe it would be better if we found something to do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's start by meeting the Hydro Archon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good idea. Nahida gave us loads of useful information.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seeking out The Seven is probably still our best source for information at this point.

choices.text: Our journey is to find my sibling...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! The more we can learn, the better.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what do you think the Hydro Archon's like? Will we get along? Nahida said that she has "a very unique personality"... whatever that means.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: To learn about a nation's god, start with the nation's people! There seems to be some locals talking over there, let's go see if we can join the party.

response.speaker: Etienne
response.text: If you ask me, it's a tragedy how things ended for him. Clearly, he was a pretty decent person.

response.speaker: Rena
response.text: Yeah, I didn't expect that kind of ending for him... I thought he would at least fight on a little longer for his family.

response.speaker: Rena
response.text: I was expecting a sudden plot twist, but it's a pity that it never happened... Still, his story is quite the tear-jerker...

response.speaker: Etienne
response.text: Uh, excuse me, can I help you two? I couldn't help but notice you standing here listening.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Hi! We're travelers new to Fontaine, and we had something we wanted to ask, but you seemed to be really busy talking about some kind of play, so we didn't want to interrupt.

response.speaker: Etienne
response.text: A "play"? Oh no, no... We're talking about something that really happened. In fact, it's a case that was just heard a few days ago.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Like a real trial? But the way you were talking about it and the words you used just now made it sound like some kind of story...

response.speaker: Rena
response.text: Well, good tales are often based on true stories, aren't they? And what you see in reality may also be someone deliberately putting on an act while harboring ulterior motives...

response.speaker: Rena
response.text: Whether something is true or not simply isn't that important. The main thing is whether the story being acted out on the stage is splendid enough.

response.speaker: Rena
response.text: Oh, but it looks like you're not from around here! You probably don't know that the Fontaine Court of Justice is called the Opera Epiclese, or more commonly known as just "the opera house."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So they see trials as a sort of "opera"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, uh... shouldn't court cases be treated a little more seriously than that? Not to question Fontaine's way of doing things, it's just that putting someone on trial is usually a very serious thing...

response.speaker: Rena
response.text: Hehe, no worries. Other visitors to Fontaine have wondered the same thing. You could say that we just don't want to waste the moving stories behind those cases.

response.speaker: Rena
response.text: And as for your worries about whether the cases are treated with due reverence, we have the absolutely just and honorable Chief Justice Neuvillette...

response.speaker: Rena
response.text: As well as the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, a machine created by the Archon. Between the machine and the Chief Justice, false charges and injustice are a thing of the past now.

choices.text: A judgment device created by the Archon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Oratrice? Is it some kind of machine too? Paimon's curious... We should check it out if we get the chance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, Paimon almost forgot to ask you our question! Do you know what we should do if we want to meet the Hydro Archon?

response.speaker: Etienne
response.text: Oh, that's easy! Just go to the opera house. Lady Furina practically lives there, you could definitely say it's her biggest passion.

response.speaker: Rena
response.text: Ah, I think what they mean is that they wish to speak with the Archon personally.

response.speaker: Rena
response.text: In that case, I'm afraid it's going to be a tad more difficult. You'll have to make an appointment well in advance, and it'll depend on whether or not she has any timeslots available.

choices.text: Make an appointment?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Is the Hydro Archon super busy taking care of official stuff? Wait, didn't you say that she's always at the opera house?

response.speaker: Etienne
response.text: No, no, Lady Furina seldom takes an interest with the nation's affairs. The reason it's difficult to make an appointment is simply because she's incredibly popular.

response.speaker: Rena
response.text: That's right, after all, she is the Archon. Though she may tend to get a little dramatic from time to time, people can't get enough of her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, first time Paimon's ever heard of an Archon being described that way before...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah wait, Paimon gets it now! The Hydro Archon is kinda like a big celebrity here, right?

response.speaker: Etienne
response.text: Yeah, I suppose you could say that. Heh, perhaps you could even say our "mascot."

response.speaker: Rena
response.text: Hang on, this is still Fontaine's Archon you're talking about. You should show some more respect!

response.speaker: Etienne
response.text: Yes, you're right. I guess I should at least try to be a little more respectful in front of visitors. Otherwise, I might get arrested and find myself face to face with Monsieur Neuvillette.

response.speaker: Rena
response.text: Haha, come on... Sure, there's a lot of laws here, but nobody's going to be arrested for saying something disrespectful about the Hydro Archon.

choices.text: Seems the people of Fontaine really like the Hydro Archon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, I think we get it, thank you! At least we now know that we can find the Hydro Archon at the opera house.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But who knows how long making an appointment will take... Guess we could have a look around the city in the meantime.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}, what are you looking over there for?

choices.text: There's a girl over there...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, maybe something's the matter... *gasp* She isn't going to jump into the water, is she?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Maybe we'd better go check on her.

choices.text: She's been standing alone for quite some time...
But they don't appear to revere her.
Timeslots?
So this is the "Nation of Justice"...
And also to find the truth.
It's even more impressive than I expected.

talks.objective: Talk to the young woman by the water

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, hello there! Excuse me! Are you alright?
...Huh?
Ah, I'm fine... Thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, okay then. We just noticed that you seemed to be worried about something.
About many things, actually... But there's nothing I can do but just keep my troubles to myself.
I was just reminiscing about a place my brother and I would play when we were kids. It was just atop that hill over there, see?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, you're pointing at the sea... Wait, are you saying that you and your brother lived in the water?

choices.text: Maybe they're mermaids?

response.text: Though people call the waters around Fontaine a "sea," it's actually just an inland lake that's filled with fresh water.
And though I can still see that hill clearly in my memories, now it's been completely submerged.
He would skip and jump, tossing sand in the wind... The sun shone brightly and the air was filled with the scent of the sea.
But now the water is gradually swallowing our memories...
It won't be long before it swallows us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, sorry, Paimon doesn't really get what you mean.
Ah, I don't believe we've had the pleasure of meeting. Are you Lynette's new friends?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and you are...
Thanks for looking after my sister, she often comes here to reminisce about our childhood, that's all. There's no need for any concern.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Ah, allow me to introduce myself. I'm Lyney, and this is my sister, Lynette. If I had to guess, I'd say you must be travelers from abroad.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Nice to meet you, Paimon is Paimon, and this is {NICKNAME}. We just arrived in Fontaine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We were just talking with your sister, uh... even though we didn't really get what she was saying.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Hmm, I see. It's unusual for Lynette to be so willing to talk with anyone, in fact, she seldom speaks at all. I'm usually the only one she ever talks to.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, really? Then you two are just like us! Paimon's always the one talking for some reason.

choices.text: There's hardly anything left for me to say with you around, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh! So that's how you think it is?

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: I also think my brother can be too talkative at times.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Ah, hehe... Seems you were right, Paimon. We are quite similar.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what did Lynette mean just now when she said that the water is engulfing your memories, and that it won't be long before it engulfs you too?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Ah, that... It's from a prophecy that's been circulating in Fontaine for some time now.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Well, I suppose "prophecy" isn't exactly the right word, because that implies a certain amount of uncertainty. There's no doubt about what's happening in Fontaine now...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh? What's happening in Fontaine?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Where to begin? Hmm...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Ah, let's put that question on hold for a moment. We still haven't formally greeted each other yet, have we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Did all the introductions earlier not count?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: #Hello, {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: Hello, Lyney.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: And hello, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Why didn't Paimon get a handshake? You're not poking fun at Paimon, are you!?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Haha, please don't take offense. Just consider it a sort of etiquette we have here in Fontaine when making new friends. You should remember it, it might prove useful...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, alright then... Well, Paimon's just happy to have a local friend now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By the way, we were just getting ready to go to the opera house to meet the Hydro Archon. Would you be able to show us the way?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: So you're going to see Lady Furina? No problem at all. In fact, I was planning to go to the opera house later myself. I'll gladly take you once I finish things here.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Please follow me.

choices.text: It's a pleasure to meet you.
Because you always steal all my lines.
Or a fantastical race from Fontaine?

talks.objective: Follow Lyney

dialogues.speaker: Etienne
dialogues.text: But where would I move to? Snezhnaya? Liyue?

talks.objective: Follow Lyney

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Uh, you said you were going to see Lady Furina? Well, it seems Lady Furina has come to see you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? So... she's the Hydro Archon? But how did she know we were looking for her?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: My dear people, rich and poor, those with cup in hand and those with nothing at all, raise your glasses in celebration! If you don't have one, then just raise your hand in lieu.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: #As you can all see, two unfamiliar travelers have arrived in our nation. Come, let us make a toast in honor of this Traveler and {M#his}{F#her} companion who have journeyed here from distant lands!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh...? Is she talking about us?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Nobody here seems to be holding a glass...)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I've long heard of the turmoil and chaos you've left in your wake as you visited other nations, but I welcome you nevertheless... No, I have come to receive you personally.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Fear is for insignificant cowards. I am a god, and I will never entertain the notion of such meaningless wariness. You can be rest assured, I see clearly your sincerity.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Of course, seeking an audience with me is the most sensible thing to do. It will allow you to truly behold my power and witness my authority. Intelligent people always gather under the correct banner.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I, Focalors, hereby welcome you to the nation of Hydro and acknowledge the value and significance of your trip. Now, you may rejoice in this!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, finding the Archon was easy enough...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Paimon still can't believe it... It feels like we've only been here for a few minutes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But the Hydro Archon's entrance was, uh... How should Paimon describe it...? A little over the top?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahem... Uh, Miss Hydro Archon... How did you know we were coming?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Ah, I see. As outlanders, you inevitably lack even some of the most basic understanding. Don't forget that even the gods can be divided into the mediocre and the excellent. I suppose it's only natural for you to be awestruck by my abilities.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: You had best stop and consider... do you really have the noble qualities and etiquette necessary to communicate with a god? All it takes is a flick of my finger for me to know everything about you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, talk about sounding high and mighty...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Feels like she can't get over herself...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh? What's with these looks? Perhaps the welcoming ceremony still isn't enough? Hmm, what else should I say then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, is she waiting for us to start talking?

dialogues.speaker: Rena
dialogues.text: Wow, I didn't expect to see Lady Furina here. What a surprise!

dialogues.speaker: Rena
dialogues.text: #Wait, does this mean they're the "Legendary {F#Blonde}{M#Blond} Traveler"!? How did I not notice before?

dialogues.speaker: Etienne
dialogues.text: Hey, what's all the commotion? Oh, is that Lady Furina? Is there some kinda drama going on?

dialogues.speaker: Lectoure
dialogues.text: #Of course! That's the {F#Blonde}{M#Blond} Traveler, the one all those stories are about. Lady Furina came here to personally see {M#him}{F#her}... Oh, I bet this is going to be the duel of the century!

dialogues.speaker: Etienne
dialogues.text: Oh! I've got to see this! I knew Lady Furina would never disappoint!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Ahaha! Yes, but don't get too excited now... My dear believers and spectators alike tend to get quite rowdy, and despite the noise, I've come to tolerate all their ruckus.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: You may consider this my reward to all of you! I have determined that there will be an epic duel between myself and this traveler from another land, just as you were hoping to see!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? Now she wants to fight? Aren't we getting a little ahead of ourselves?

choices.text: ...Bring it on.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Hmm? Hmph! A—Are you not afraid? Might I remind you that this is a duel against the divine!

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: What are you trying to do, Traveler? Provoking a god in front of her people?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: #Ahem, stand down, Clorinde. I admire {M#his}{F#her} bravery, few have the courage to draw their sword against a god. {M#He}{F#She} is obviously a true warrior.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Unfortunately, people nowadays only crave to be thrilled, and a mere duel will not slake their thirst for excitement!

response.speaker: Lectoure
response.text: ...Yeah, she's right. Just a duel wouldn't be all that interesting...

response.speaker: Etienne
response.text: On Erinnyes, criminals are always requesting duels to defend their honor. They're getting a bit old, to tell the truth.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: You see... then as the god of justice, I shall face this Traveler in another kind of duel... a duel in court!

response.speaker: Lectoure
response.text: Whoa! Oooh, alright, now that'll be worth seeing!

response.speaker: Etienne
response.text: Right, this is Fontaine, after all. With such a grand opera house, it would be a pity not to use it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why do you care so much about the crowd's reactions? Seems you've spent a little too much time in the opera house...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Besides, how exactly do you plan to have a duel in court? You mean you're going to put us on trial?

choices.text: And we haven't committed any crimes.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Hehe. Oh, we have reason to put you on trial. It's obvious, isn't it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Obvious?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: According to Fontaine law, no one is permitted to release any flying objects within Fontaine city limits during the first three days of each month. You are clearly guilty of violating this law, no?

response.speaker: Etienne
response.text: Oh! So that's what they've done wrong. That's our Lady Furina, no one knows the laws of Fontaine like she does.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You call that obvious? What kind of law is that!? Wait, "flying object"...? You mean Paimon!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Uh...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Precisely. Now, if you two have no objections, then in the name of the Hydro Archon, I order your arrest.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: My apologies, Lady Furina. I don't mean to spoil the fun, but if you would allow me to interject...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: ...I don't think that Paimon here meets the definition of a "flying object."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You tell her, Lyney! Finally, someone who's not crazy... How could anyone call Paimon a flying object!?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Ah, Great Magician Lyney, my beloved citizen. I'll permit you to object, but how exactly do you plan to prove your claim?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Hehe, as a magician who just rained on your parade, I naturally should shoulder the responsibility of "saving the show"...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: So, with such an audience gathered here, allow me to perform a trick for everyone.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: (Snap!)

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Tada~

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Waa! What's that on Paimon's back? Hey, when did you do that!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Ah, when Lyney patted you on the back...)

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: There. As you can all clearly see, Paimon should be classified as, well, something like a balloon. This rope has been in the Traveler's hand all along, it was just that no one could see it before.

response.speaker: Rena
response.text: Huh, you call that magic? You've got to be joking...

response.speaker: Etienne
response.text: Hahaha, I thought it was pretty good. Nice one!

response.speaker: Lectoure
response.text: Huh, I'm not sure what to think. It seems Lady Furina's charges no longer hold water...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Hah! Hahahaha...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Amusing. Very amusing, Lyney. Just the sort of unexpected twist that I enjoy. With you here, today's performance can finally be called complete.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Performance? You see all this as a performance?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: In which case, consider the matter of your trial resolved. The god of justice will not bring charges against an innocent person.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: But when there are valid grounds, I will not only judge travelers from abroad...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: But even the gods of other lands, hehehe...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I look forward to seeing your upcoming performance at the opera house, Mister Lyney and Miss Lynette. That's enough for now. Toodle-oo~

choices.text: We literally just arrived here.
(Fighting gods? I've got a resumé.)

talks.objective: Talk to Lyney

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And just like that, she's gone. Well, that's the most unpredictable archon Paimon's ever seen... We never even had a chance to ask her anything, but that's a problem for future Paimon! That whole scene just now was really...

choices.text: Thanks for bailing us out, Lyney.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Don't mention it. I just happened to remember that there was such a law, so I did a little preparation — just in case. I didn't think it would actually come in handy.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: So, now do you see what kind of god Lady Furina is?

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: She can be a bit confusing at times, but she is still amenable to reason.

choices.text: Yeah, confusing is a good way to put it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, Paimon had no idea you were a magician, Lyney. It sounded like you'll be performing at the opera house, right?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Haha, I just know a few simple tricks I use to make a living. Lynette is my assistant.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: It will actually be my first time performing on the most prestigious stage in Fontaine, the opera house.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But isn't the opera house where criminal trials are held in Fontaine?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: When there are no public trials being held, the opera house hosts a variety of other performances. To the people of Fontaine, the line between a trial and a performance can be a little blurred...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: And speaking of performances, I would be remiss to forgo this opportunity gifted by fate. Might I invite the two of you to see my performance?

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: My brother's always excited to make new friends.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, sure. We don't really have anything to do now, and we wanted to go to the opera house anyway.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I would be delighted.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Splendid! In that case, why don't we go together? I'll show you the way. I just have something to take care of first...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is there any way I can help?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: You really mean it? Then I'll take you up on your offer.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: This is a magical item known as a "Magic Pocket." Perhaps you can help me distribute them to the people here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What are they going to use it for?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: About that, hmm... You asked me before about the prophecy, right? Let me start by telling you a little more about what it entails.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I'm not sure exactly when it began, but a prophecy has been circulating around Fontaine...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: It says that every person in Fontaine is born with "sin." No matter how the Nation of Justice holds trial after trial, this sin cannot be absolved.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Until one day, the water levels in Fontaine will rise, and the sinful people will slowly be drowned...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: In the end, the people will all be dissolved into the waters, and only the Hydro Archon will remain, weeping on her throne... Only then will the sins of the people of Fontaine be washed away.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds pretty gloomy... Why are people in Fontaine born with sin? What is that supposed to mean?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: There are lots of guesses... Some say that the ancestors of Fontaine stole the power of the seas, and stirred its wrath.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Others say that the people of Fontaine never heeded the first Hydro Archon's warnings, and offended Celestia...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But, here in Fontaine, evidence is what matters. There hasn't been concrete evidence for any of these claims, so they can only be regarded as conjecture.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If even the people in Fontaine don't know what sin they committed, wouldn't it be better just to ignore the prophecy completely? Why bother feeling guilty all the time?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That's exactly what the people did at first. But... in the last few years, the water levels in Fontaine have actually started rising.

choices.text: "But now the water is engulfing our memories..."

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Many places have already been completely submerged and now lie beneath the sea.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Many people carry on with their lives as before and shrug it off as a "natural phenomenon," but my family and I think that the people of Fontaine shouldn't ignore the possibility, which would end up sentencing them to death.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: We hope that at least the people who reside near the waterfront can move away before it's too late, so we've started distributing Magic Pockets to them.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: As a magical item, these Magic Pockets have an astonishing capacity. I'm sure they will come in handy when people are moving their belongings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon gets it! It's like preparing for a rainy day... but this is more than a bit of rain!

choices.text: If the prophecy is true...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Hmm, perhaps only absolute power could ever contend with such a catastrophe. Hehe, but who knows? We're just tiny specks in the grand scheme of things.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Now, if you'd like to help, then please give these Magic Pockets to anyone nearby. Be sure to convince them to take it, regardless of what they say.

choices.text: Then is there no way to prevent the disaster?
"It won't be long before it engulfs us."
Is she really that reasonable?
Did you know that was going to happen?

talks.objective: Distribute Magic Pockets to the nearby residents

dialogues.speaker: Etienne
dialogues.text: #So you're the {F#blonde}{M#blond} Traveler that everyone's been talking about. My apologies for not recognizing you earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Etienne
dialogues.text: Oh, a Magic Pocket...? Seems you really thought of everything. I guess it's better to prepare for the worst and hope for the best...

dialogues.speaker: Etienne
dialogues.text: Thanks. Please also thank the magician on my behalf when you get the chance.

talks.objective: Distribute Magic Pockets to the nearby residents

dialogues.speaker: Galathee
dialogues.text: Huh? Ah, I don't want that thing. Way I see it, if the prophecy's true, it's still gonna be a long time before the water can cover everything.

dialogues.speaker: Galathee
dialogues.text: Life is all about living in the moment. What use is there in worrying about the future all the time? We'll cross that bridge when we get to it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You should still take it, you never know when it will come in handy.

dialogues.speaker: Galathee
dialogues.text: Oh, alright... fine. Thanks. It's just that... if I start moving, that means I've already given up on the life I have now. I'd really rather not...

talks.objective: Distribute Magic Pockets to the nearby residents

dialogues.speaker: Augereau
dialogues.text: What's this... So you also believe in the prophecy? Hehe, keep it, I won't have any use for it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? You mean you don't believe in the prophecy?

dialogues.speaker: Augereau
dialogues.text: No, no, I believe in the prophecy, but I also believe in another story.

dialogues.speaker: Augereau
dialogues.text: The story says that people once lived in the ocean. They were one with the ocean and couldn't live apart from it.

dialogues.speaker: Augereau
dialogues.text: But as time wore on, people desired to live on land and developed blood vessels, encapsulating the sea within their bodies. Thus could people set foot on land.

dialogues.speaker: Augereau
dialogues.text: So if you ask me, when the water rises and takes us all, it'll be like we're going home.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, we hadn't heard that one before... But, people can't live underwater, they'll die... You should probably still take it.

dialogues.speaker: Augereau
dialogues.text: Ah, alright, I'll take it. I guess I just feel that being "dissolved into the water" doesn't necessarily mean death.

dialogues.speaker: Etienne
dialogues.text: Hey, how about we get some tickets to the next trial?

dialogues.speaker: Rena
dialogues.text: Hmm, I think we'd better wait and see what kind of case it is first.

talks.objective: Talk to Lyney

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Oh? You already handed out all of the Magic Pockets? That was fast. So, what did people have to say? I bet you heard some, ah, interesting opinions...

choices.text: No kidding...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Yes, but that will change once disaster strikes. I know they'll change their minds, so it's only right to help them prepare.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is there anything else you need to do before we leave?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Yes, one last thing. I have the Magic Pockets made by a workshop in the Court of Fontaine. Since we're out and about, I was thinking about bringing him some more materials.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you want to collect materials? Just tell us what the materials look like and we'll help. Many hands make light work!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Ah, that would be much appreciated. We'll need some Romaritime Flowers, I remember seeing them near the waterfront on the east side of the harbor.

choices.text: Many are quite stubborn.

talks.objective: Collect materials used to make Magic Pockets
Collect materials used to make Magic Pockets

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Whaaaat?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}? Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Charlotte!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's Charlotte!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I never guessed I'd bump into you while riding the aquabus. In the story of my life, this is big news!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: What are you doing in Fontaine? I didn't hear anything about you paying us a visit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's quite the coincidence! But as Travelers, we're always on the move. It's not surprising that nobody knew we were coming.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, though we still have no idea how the Hydro Archon knew about us... Oh! Let Paimon introduce you to our new friends!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Oh, no need for introductions, Paimon. I would recognize the Great Magician Lyney and his assistant Lynette anywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I wouldn't be much of a reporter if I didn't know who they were. It's a pleasure to meet you! I'm Charlotte, a reporter for The Steambird.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Nice to meet you. From The Steambird, huh? We've often relied on your paper to promote our performances.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: It's an honor to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, now that everyone knows each other, Fontaine suddenly doesn't feel like such an unfamiliar place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what have you been up to lately, Charlotte? Any big news?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Not too much... when there isn't any breaking news, I mainly cover the trials at the opera house...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: You can still manage to keep readers' attention as long as you tell things from a clever enough angle, even if it's the same old topics.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: For example, reporting on how a scammer once deceived vulnerable girls into relationships, or how a financial criminal was once so poor that they ate a single piece of bread for five days...

choices.text: That... would definitely get my attention.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: *sigh* You're right, seems you know me pretty well. What I'm really after is exclusive, sensational news pieces that could shake the country. These smaller stories are a waste of my talents.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Oh, I just remembered... I've been following a case lately... well, a series of cases, actually...

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: You mean the "serial disappearances of young women" case?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: That's right. These stories are the talk of the town right now, and it's probably the most mysterious case we've ever seen.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: If I'm the first with a draft ready to publish when the case is finally cracked, and it's the headline story in The Steambird...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: When that happens, I bet all the other reporters will shed tears of envy. I've already gathered all kinds of materials, I just can't wait for the truth to be revealed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what is the "serial disappearances of young women" case? You mean the culprit hasn't been found?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: That's right. The first missing girl case happened almost twenty years ago.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: And ever since, after a period of time, another girl disappears. What the cases have in common is that the girls are all of a similar age, and that they've all vanished without a trace.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: But the scariest part is that to this day, none of the girls have ever been found.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Many suspects have been arrested over the years in connection with this case. But shortly after each arrest, another disappearance would always happen.

choices.text: Then there must be more than one criminal at work.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Yes, it's possible. But either way, I believe that every case has some precise truth behind it, waiting to be exposed.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Yes, I agree. And at the very least, the families of those missing girls deserve some sort of explanation.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I just imagined for a second what I would do if Lynette were to suddenly disappear... I'd pay any price to get her back and then find a way to track down the culprit.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Please don't imagine that, Lyney.

choices.text: Maybe there are copycat criminals?
But that's not really the kind of news you're after.

talks.objective: Collect materials used to make Magic Pockets

dialogues.speaker: Augereau
dialogues.text: What do you think? Pretty interesting story, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Galathee
dialogues.text: I really can't imagine what it would be like if things changed...

talks.objective: Talk to Lyney

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You made quick work of that, I can tell you're an experienced traveler. I've also finished collecting a few here.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Maybe next time you'll feel like helping too, Lynette.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: No way. I'm in power-saving mode today. Otherwise, I fear I may not have any energy left for the performance at the opera house.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: *sigh* Fine, though the performance is still a long way off. Now that we're finished here, we should get ready to head back to the Court of Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So we're going to the Court of Fontaine before we head to the opera house? Good, Paimon wants a tour of Fontaine's largest city and try—

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Wait... Shh! Have you noticed that person over there? The young girl...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's wrong with her? Paimon didn't notice anything.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Heh, she's obviously a thief.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Magicians and thieves practice similar methods. We divert attention, and a distracted audience is one that won't discover what you're really doing.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Watch her movements carefully...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, he's right!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Shh! Keep your voice down... We need to think of a way to catch her, but it seems she's very alert. Perhaps we should split up.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You two can ride the lift over there and wait up top. I bet that'll be her escape route if she tries to run.

choices.text: Understood.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Alright, let's go.

choices.text: Leave it to me.

talks.objective: Go to the top of the lift to cut off the thief's escape

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is the spot where Lyney wanted us to wait.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, look! Isn't that her!?

choices.text: Get ready to stop her!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no, did she notice us? She started running the other direction!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What should we do? Should we chase her?

choices.text: Our job is to block this path.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, you're right. She might also be trying to lure us away.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You wait, but there's no sign of the thief...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nothing's happened for a while now. Paimon wonders if Lyney caught the thief...

choices.text: Seems there's no reason for us to stay here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, let's go.

choices.text: Let's go find Lyney.
The rest is up to Lyney.
Time to make the arrest!

talks.objective: Talk to Lyney

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Are you sure that's all she took? You should check to make sure you're not missing anything else.

dialogues.speaker: Lectoure
dialogues.text: No, that was all. I can't thank you enough, I didn't notice a thing earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Lectoure
dialogues.text: Anyway, I should be going now. Thanks again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, were you returning what the thief had stolen?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: That's right, pity I wasn't able to catch her. She distracted me by dropping the things she stole on the ground. By the time I looked back, she was already gone.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: I saw the general direction she went, but Lyney twisted his ankle, and I needed to make sure he was okay.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? Did you get hurt, Lyney?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I'll be alright. It's just a twisted ankle, that's all. In fact, it's feeling better already.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: If you want to play at being a hero, at least try not to get hurt doing it. Imagine what would happen if you managed to derail our performance as a result.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Haha... You're right, you're right! Sorry, Lynette.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: *sigh* I have to admit, that thief was even more skilled than I had anticipated.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But at least we were able to get the stolen items back, so it wasn't a complete failure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a slippery little thief... Guess things turned out alright in the end though. Lyney's initiative paid off!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Alright, let's put this little detour behind us. We should go to the Court of Fontaine now.

talks.objective: Ride the aquabus to the Court of Fontaine

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? Hey, we're almost there. Look!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Well, I really enjoyed chatting with you. Life should be full of pleasant little surprises like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, us as well! The ride went by too quickly.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Ah! I have an interview to get to. I should get going before I'm late.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, Paimon hopes we can chat again soon, Charlotte. See ya!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Hehe, bye now. Be sure to stop by and see me at The Steambird when you have time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a tough job... always running around and interviewing everyone. Well, where should we go now?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: If you don't mind, how about we stop by my home first? Besides, I still have all the materials we collected.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure, we wouldn't mind at all. This city is so huge, Paimon wouldn't know where to start anyway.

talks.objective: Ride the aquabus to the Court of Fontaine

dialogues.speaker: Bounty Notice
dialogues.text: Wanted: Name unknown. Seeking any and all relevant information.

dialogues.speaker: Bounty Notice
dialogues.text: Male, Fontainian. One leg is a prosthetic replacement. Known alias: Mr. Sawleg. Has conducted illegal performances at Romaritime Station, resulting in a disruption of public order.

dialogues.speaker: Bounty Notice
dialogues.text: Rewards are available for information leading to the capture of this individual. If you have any related information, please contact the Maison Gardiennage.

talks.objective: Ride the aquabus to the Court of Fontaine
Ride the aquabus to the Court of Fontaine

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Continue Reading

dialogues.speaker: Notice to Travelers
dialogues.text: Attention all visitors! Any and all dueling within Fontaine will require application and registration with the appropriate authorities.

dialogues.speaker: Notice to Travelers
dialogues.text: Private, unapproved duels are strictly prohibited. Any participants will be punished to the fullest extent of the law. Any and all losses and damages resulting from unauthorized private duels will be borne by the participants.

dialogues.speaker: Addendum
dialogues.text: Arrests made by the Maison Gardiennage are not considered duels or dueling behavior! If you wish to uphold your honor, you may apply for a duel during the trial process. Refrain from any last-ditch resistance if you wish to avoid meaningless losses.

talks.objective: Go to the Court of Fontaine

dialogues.speaker: Romaritime Harbor Bulletin Board
dialogues.text: This bulletin board has been specially set up by the Harbormaster of Romaritime Harbor to publicize all important matters in and around the harbor. Any questions may also be posted here.

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Notice to Travelers
dialogues.text: The Maison Gardiennage would like to remind you that Romaritime Harbor is near the desert, and large numbers of illegal individuals calling themselves Eremites have been active nearby. Merchants passing through should remain vigilant.

dialogues.speaker: Notice to Travelers
dialogues.text: If you see something, say something! Contact the Maison Gardiennage to deal with any suspicious persons.

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Leave

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It seems we have to use Hydro to collect Romaritime Flowers.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You continue talking on the aquabus, and before you know it, you are arriving at your destination.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After settling matters in Sumeru, you approach the border with Fontaine...
